svg.text: Task 1(a) — Logical Design: Sales & Returns Data Warehouse (Fact Constellation with Conformed Dimensions)
Design notes
1. Fact constellation (galaxy schema). DATE, PRODUCT, CUSTOMER, BRANCH and
PROMOTION are conformed — identical keys and identical meaning in both facts.
2. DATE_DIM is a role-playing dimension, referenced three times: order date
(SALES_FACT), return date and original order date (RETURNS_FACT). Expose it
as views ORDER_DATE_DIM and RETURN_DATE_DIM for the BI layer.
3. Grain — SALES_FACT: one row per item line per order. RETURNS_FACT: one row
per returned item line. The PK is the minimal key that enforces that grain;
dimension keys are NOT NULL FKs and are indexed, but are not part of the PK.
4. Natural keys are marked NK, not FK — there is no parent table in the warehouse.
† CUSTOMER_DIM is Type 2, so customer_id is deliberately not unique:
UNIQUE (customer_id, effective_start_date).
5. Every dimension is seeded with key = -1 'Unknown' for dirty source data.
PROMOTION_DIM additionally seeds key = 0 'No Promotion', so a non-promotional
sale is never confused with an unresolvable promotion reference.
6. Cost and gross-profit measures are omitted: the source system records no cost
column. Profitability is analysed through discount leakage and net-of-returns
revenue instead.
7. Green text marks a change from the previous draft.
Legend
PK
Primary key (enforces the declared grain)
FK
Foreign key to a dimension — NOT NULL, indexed
NK
Natural / business key from the source system
DD
Degenerate dimension (operational reference number)
